prerequisites: Differential and integral calculus of functions of one variable

learning_outcomes.text: Acquaint students with the basics of differential and integral calculus of functions of several variables, enabling them to attend engineering courses and deal with engineering problems.
Students will be made familiar with differential and integral calculus of more variables.
Students will be able to apply this knowledge in various engineering tasks.
After completing the course students will be prepared for further study of physics, mechanics and other technical disciplines.

syllabus_topics: Functions in more variables: basic definitions, limit of a function, continuous functions, partial derivative
Higher-order partial derivatives, gradient of a function, derivative in a direction, first-order and higher-order differentials, tangent plane to the graph of a function in two variables
Taylor polynomial, local maxima and minima of functions in several variables
Relative maxima and minima, absolute maxima and minima
Double and triple integral, Fubini's theorem: calculation on normal sets
Substitution theorem, cylindrical and spherical co-ordinates
Applications of double and triple integrals
Curves and their orientations, first-type line integral and its applications
Second-type line integral and its applications, Green's theorem
Line integrals independent of the integration path, potential, the nabla and delta operators, divergence and curl of a vector field
Surfaces (parametric equations, orienting of a surface), first-type surface integral and its applications
Second-type surface integral and its applications, Gauss' theorem and Stokes' theorem
Calculating improper integrals, applications of the Riemann integral
Plotting of the graph of a function of more variables (given by explicit, implicit or parametric equations)
Extrema of functions of more variables

assessment_methods.method: Written part of examination (Problem 1: Basic properties of functions of several variables: domains, partial derivatives, gradient)
Written part of examination (Problem 2: Differential calculus of functions of several variables)
Written part of examination (Problem 3: Double and triple integral)
Written part of examination (Problem 4: Line and surface integral)
Oral part of examination (Discussion based on the written test)
Oral part of examination (Possible theoretic question)
Oral part of examination (Possible simple problem to be solved straight away)

assessment_rules: Students must achieve at least 6 points in each of the two written seminar tests to obtain course-unit credit; these tests are worth a maximum of 12 points each. If the minimum is not met, a repeat test is possible during the first two weeks of the examination period. The final exam consists of a written part (maximum 75 points) and an oral part (maximum 25 points). For the written part, students must solve four problems. The final classification is based on a total of 100 points: 0-49 points is F, 50-59 points is E, 60-69 points is D, 70-79 points is C, 80-89 points is B, and 90-100 points is A.
